title: must mustn't don't need to
subtitle: I must / I mustn't / I don't need to
summary: Use must for what is necessary, mustn't for what is wrong to do, and don't need to for what is not necessary.

lesson.heading: You must see it
lesson.text: Two friends are standing outside a cinema. One of them points at the poster for tonight's film and says: 'It's a fantastic film. You must see it.' **I must** (do something) = I need to do it.

examples.text: I'm very hungry. I **must eat** something.
It's a fantastic film. You **must see** it.
The windows are very dirty. We **must clean** them.

lesson.heading: The form
lesson.note: must is the same for every subject and takes no to: he **must go**, not ~~he musts go~~ or ~~he must to go~~.

lesson.heading: For the past: had to
lesson.text: For the past (yesterday, last week etc.), we use **had to ...**, not must.

examples.text: I was very hungry. I **had to eat** something.
We **had to walk** home last night. There were no buses.

lesson.heading: mustn't
lesson.text: **mustn't** = must not. **I mustn't** (do something) = it is necessary *not* to do it, it is the wrong thing to do. In an art gallery a small child reaches up to a painting, and her mother says: 'You mustn't touch the pictures.'

examples.note: = I must remember to phone her

lesson.heading: don't need to
lesson.text: **I don't need** (to do something) = it is not necessary. You can also say **don't have to ...**

examples.text: I **don't need to go** yet. I can stay a little longer.
You **don't need to shout**. I can hear you OK.
I **don't have to go** yet. I can stay a little longer.

left.label: don't need to (it is not necessary)
examples: You **don't need to go**. You can stay here if you want.

right.label: mustn't (it is the wrong thing to do)
examples: You **mustn't go**. You must stay here.

lesson.text: don't need to gives you a free choice; mustn't gives you no choice at all.

exercises.prompt: Marilyn is a very interesting person. You ___ her.
exercises.explanation: must + verb says that something is necessary.

exercises.prompt: My hands are dirty. I ___ them.
exercises.explanation: I need to do it: I must wash them.

exercises.prompt: Match the sentences that mean the same thing.

pairs.left: We can leave the meeting early.
pairs.right: We don't need to stay until the end.

pairs.left: We must leave the meeting early.
pairs.right: We can't stay until the end.

pairs.left: We mustn't leave the meeting early.
pairs.right: We must stay until the end.

pairs.left: We had to leave the meeting early.
pairs.right: We couldn't stay until the end.

pairs.left: We don't need to leave the meeting early.
pairs.right: We can stay until the end.

exercises.explanation: It is necessary now, so: I must go.

exercises.prompt: I went to London by train last week. The train was full and ___ stand all the way.
exercises.explanation: Last week is the past, so we use had to, not must.

exercises.prompt: We have a lot of time. We ___.
exercises.explanation: It is not necessary: we don't need to hurry.

exercises.prompt: Keep these papers in a safe place. You ___ them.
exercises.explanation: It would be the wrong thing to do: you mustn't lose them.

exercises.prompt: The lights are still on and you are leaving. Warn your friend.
exercises.answer: We mustn't forget to turn off the lights before we leave.

exercises.prompt: The restaurant won't be busy tonight. We ___ reserve a table.
exercises.explanation: It is not necessary, so we use don't need to.

exercises.prompt: You ___ tell Sue what happened. I don't want her to know.
exercises.explanation: It is the wrong thing to do, so: you mustn't tell Sue.

exercises.statement: I was very hungry. I must eat something.
exercises.explanation: I was very hungry. I had to eat something. For the past we use had to.

categories: It is the wrong thing to do

items.text: I must hurry or I'll be late.
I don't need to go yet. I can stay a little longer.
The windows are very dirty. We must clean them.
You don't need to shout. I can hear you OK.
I mustn't forget to phone Jane.
